subject: Next steps: DataCove evaluation on Redwood - onboarding & scoring plan
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@datacove.ai>, Emily Chen <emily@datacove.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up + proposed eval onboarding for DataCove (post-demo)

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — great conversation. Below is a short recap and proposed next steps so we can get a customer-specific eval running on Redwood quickly. I tried to keep this lean so your engineering/legal teams can scan for dependencies.

Recap (call):
- Primary goal: validate model quality on DataCove extraction tasks (medical claim field extraction) and measure latency/cost tradeoffs for batch inference.
- Success metric: entity F1 on labeled dev set (DataCove-provided) and human judgment delta vs current production model.
- Constraints: PHI-equivalent data, so Private deployment or dedicated pools with KMS required for any raw data.

Proposed immediate plan (2-week soak):
1) Data format & sample: you provide a 1k–2k sample (anonymized) JSONL with fields: id, prompt, expected (gold), and metadata. See our sample attached (datacove_eval_sample.jsonl).
2) Prompt set: include 100 representative prompts for different claim types (attached: datacove_prompt_sets.csv). We'll use these for model-conditioned scoring.
3) Automated eval run: Redwood will run 4 model variants (see model recs below) across the dataset, return token-level traces, latency/cost, and per-example scores.
4) Human eval: We'll run a 200-example blind judgment pool (you or a third-party can provide judges) using the attached scoring rubric.
5) Deliverables: evaluation report (quality table + failure modes), recommended model + quantization profile, and a runbook for production rollout.

Model recommendations (quick):
- Llama-2-Chat-13B (float16) — baseline for generation + structured extraction via prompts.
- RedQuant-13B (int8/4) — good latency/cost tradeoff for batch workloads (we'll measure quality delta).
- Instruction-tuned open model (vicuna-13b-instruct) — useful as a low-cost baseline for high-recall extractions.
- Fallback: smaller 7B comb for ultra-low-latency endpoints.

Data & compliance note:
Because you're handling sensitive fields, we'll restrict the test data to an isolated dedicated pool and enable KMS envelope encryption. If you prefer, we can instead provide an on-prem Redwood Private image for a fully air-gapped run (longer setup lead time).

Next concrete asks from DataCove to start: (preferably by EOD Friday)
- A sanitized JSONL sample (1k rows) with expected outputs
- Confirmation of whether you require on-prem / VPC / dedicated-host mode
- Any scoring preferences beyond the attached rubric (precision-weighted, cost-sensitive scoring, etc.)

Attachments: datacove_prompt_sets.csv; datacove_eval_sample.jsonl

Thanks — I'll schedule a 30-min onboarding next week to walk through the eval template if that helps.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priom@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

---
Priyom@redwood.ai
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@datacove.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Chen <emily@datacove.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up + proposed eval onboarding for DataCove (post-demo)

Thanks, Priyom — useful summary. A few clarifying questions before we hand over samples: 

1) Dataset schema: Can you confirm the exact JSONL fields you need and whether we should include any PHI-like flags (we will mask identifiers but keep structural metadata)?
2) Scoring: The rubric looks reasonable; we're most sensitive to false positives (precision). Can you run both F1 and a precision-weighted score and report both?
3) Models: Is RedQuant something built by Redwood or a configuration you apply to an open model? We need to understand licensing and reproducibility.
4) Environment: For the initial run we prefer a dedicated Redwood pool with KMS rather than on-prem. Who from your infra team will set the dedicated pool up and what info do you need from us?

Also, we want to see a sample output (1–2 examples) from your side for the same prompt set so stakeholders can see the schema of inference output. If you can attach that sample output and an example of the per-example report that would be perfect.

Thanks — I can get the JSONL sample ready but need the exact schema.

-Rajiv
Rajiv Menon
Head of ML, DataCove
rajiv@datacove.ai
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@datacove.ai>, Emily Chen <emily@datacove.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up + proposed eval onboarding for DataCove (post-demo)

Rajiv — great questions, answered inline below. I've attached a small sample output and a per-example report template.

1) Dataset schema (please follow exactly):
- id (string)
- prompt (string) — the instruction + context you want the model to act on
- gold (string or JSON object) — expected extraction result; if structured, send as JSON-stringified object inside the field
- tags (string) — Optional comma-separated tags for stratification (claim_type, source_system)
- jurisdiction (string) — us/eu/apac for any locale-specific checks

Note: we've included one masked sample in datacove_eval_sample.jsonl to illustrate JSON-stringified gold.

2) Scoring: we'll compute per-example precision/recall/F1 (token + span-level where applicable) and also a precision-weighted score you requested. We'll include confusion lists for high-FP examples.

3) RedQuant explanation: it's Redwood's quantization profile applied to an open-architecture 13B checkpoint (int8/4). Licensing: we only apply quantization to open checkpoints (we'll document which upstream checkpoints we used). You'll get the exact upstream model ids and hashes in the report.

4) Dedicated pool setup: our infra lead (Marcus Lin) will provision the dedicated pool. Action items for your infra/security team:
- Provide the subnet CIDR and KMS key ARN (or confirm we should use Redwood-managed KMS for the evaluation)
- Add two egress IPs to allow our provisioning agent to download the checkpoints (we can also use a signed S3 transfer if you prefer)

Sample output & per-example report: attached (per_example_report_example.csv). This shows the fields we return: id, model, output, tokens, latency_ms, cost_tokens, match_type, score_precision, score_recall, notes.

I'll have Marcus follow up with the provisioning timeline and a run command you can execute if you prefer the dedicated pool to be owned by DataCove (we can do either).

Next step: if you can share the 1k sample by Friday, Marcus and I will queue the eval and send a short note once results are uploaded to s3://redwood-evals/datacove/initial-run/.

Best,
Priyom

Attachments: per_example_report_example.csv; sample_output_2examples.jsonl
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@datacove.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Emily Chen <emily@datacove.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up + proposed eval onboarding for DataCove (post-demo)

Hey Rajiv — I'm Marcus (infra lead). Short tech notes and the provisioning checklist so you can loop in your cloud/security folks: 

Provisioning checklist (dedicated pool):
- Provide VPC subnet CIDR (we'll return an AMI/installer for the pool)
- KMS: supply AWS KMS ARN OR allow Redwood-managed KMS for the eval (customer decision)
- Egress/IPs: add 34.200.82.12 and 34.200.82.13 to allow transient bootstrap downloads (or request signed S3 transfer)
- Storage: we'll need an S3 bucket with read/write for eval artifacts or we can stage to our s3 with a pre-signed transfer.

Technical run params we recommend for initial sweep (we'll tune after first run):
- Batch size: 16 (stable for 13B on our dedicated 1xA100-80G pool)
- KV cache TTL: 30s (we'll disable cross-request caching for privacy-sensitive runs unless you approve)
- RedQuant profile: int8 dynamic + per-channel clipping. Expect ~2x speedup vs float16 with a small drop in F1 (we'll quantify).
- Timeout/latency SLO: 2500ms p95 for single-turn prompts; we can lower target for production endpoints later.

Scoring & artifacts delivered:
- We will produce: per-example JSON lines (id + model + output + latency + token_cost + score_precision + score_recall + notes)
- Human rubric (attached: scoring_rubric.md) and sample judgments (sample_judgments.csv) for transparency.

Security notes:
- All logs and token traces for this run will be disabled by default; you can opt-in to token-level traces in a private bucket if you want deeper failure-mode analysis.

I'll spin up the pool once you share the subnet/KMS choice. Priyom — let me know if you want me to host a 20-min call with their cloud security folks tomorrow.

-Marcus Lin
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0123

Attachments: scoring_rubric.md; sample_judgments.csv
